/pages/software/windows/utility/winmerge: Open-source file and folder diff and merge tool for Windows.
WinMerge shows differences between two or three files or folders with color-coded highlighting. You can merge changes selectively, compare folder trees, and view differences in binary files.
Plugin support adds syntax highlighting for code files. WinMerge integrates with most version control systems and text editors via external diff tool configuration.
/pages/software/windows/utility/vlc.html: Open-source multimedia player for Windows supporting all formats.

VLC plays virtually every audio and video format without needing to install additional codecs. The Windows build supports hardware-accelerated decoding via DXVA2 and D3D11, enabling smooth 4K and HDR playback on most PCs.
It also works as a media converter, network stream player, and screen recorder. No ads, no tracking, no subscription — VideoLAN keeps it free forever.
/pages/software/windows/utility/handbrak: Free, open-source video transcoder for Windows.

HandBrake converts video between virtually any format using industry-standard codecs like H.264, H.265, VP9, and AV1. On Windows it leverages Intel Quick Sync, AMD VCE, and NVIDIA NVENC for hardware-accelerated encoding.
Built-in presets cover web streaming, device targets, and archival quality. The batch queue lets you add multiple jobs and walk away while they process.
/pages/software/windows/productivity/thu: Free email client from Mozilla for Windows with OpenPGP support.

Thunderbird is a solid open-source email client for Windows with a native installer. It supports multiple accounts, spam filtering, message tags, and built-in OpenPGP encryption for secure email communication.
The Supernova redesign brought a unified sidebar for mail, calendar, tasks, and chat. Extensions from addons.thunderbird.net add further customization.
/pages/software/windows/productivity/not: Free, feature-rich text and code editor for Windows.
Available as a standard installer or portable zip. It starts in milliseconds and handles very large files without issue, making it a daily driver for many developers and writers.
/pages/software/windows/utility/7zip.htm: Free, open-source file archiver with high compression ratio for Windows.

7-Zip is the gold standard free archiver on Windows. It natively handles 7z, ZIP, RAR, TAR, GZIP, BZIP2, ISO, and many other formats. The 7z format achieves compression ratios significantly better than ZIP.
Right-click context menu integration makes archiving and extracting seamless. 7-Zip is open-source and free for any use — personal or commercial.
/pages/software/windows/productivity/lib: Free, open-source office suite for Windows compatible with Microsoft Office.

LibreOffice is the full-featured open-source alternative to Microsoft Office for Windows. Writer handles documents, Calc handles spreadsheets, and Impress handles presentations — all with strong DOCX/XLSX/PPTX compatibility.
The Windows installer is straightforward and creates Start Menu entries for all apps. LibreOffice also supports ODF formats, ensuring long-term document accessibility.
/pages/software/windows/productivity/kee: Offline, open-source password manager for Windows.

KeePassXC is a community fork of KeePass with a modern Qt-based UI, auto-type, browser integration via the KeePassXC-Browser extension, and TOTP support. Your password database is a single encrypted .kdbx file you control.
It integrates with Windows Credential Manager and supports YubiKey as a second factor. Because it is offline-first, there is no cloud service to breach.
/pages/software/windows/productivity/gim: GNU Image Manipulation Program — professional image editor for Windows.

GIMP is a free, professional raster image editor that runs natively on Windows. It supports layers, channels, masks, script automation, and a wide array of plugins. The UI is highly customizable with dockable dialogs.
GIMP handles tasks from photo retouching to original art creation. It is a capable Photoshop alternative for users who do not need non-destructive RAW editing workflows.
/pages/software/windows/games/wesnoth.ht: Open-source turn-based fantasy strategy game for Windows.

Battle for Wesnoth is a deep turn-based strategy game set in a high-fantasy world. It features over a dozen official campaigns, skirmish maps, and an active online multiplayer community. Units level up and carry between scenarios.
The built-in map editor and Lua scripting engine mean the modding community has produced thousands of fan-made campaigns available through the in-game add-on browser.
/pages/software/windows/games/supertuxka: Free and open-source kart racing game for Windows.

SuperTuxKart is a fun, arcade-style kart racing game featuring open-source mascots as characters. It includes over 20 tracks, multiple game modes (Grand Prix, Time Trial, Battle), and local/online multiplayer.
The game features beautiful 3D graphics, power-ups, and a full story mode. It installs cleanly on Windows and is available as a portable zip as well.
/pages/software/windows/games/openttd.ht: Open-source transport tycoon simulation game for Windows.

OpenTTD is a faithful open-source reimplementation of Transport Tycoon Deluxe. Build a transport empire using trains, buses, trucks, ships, and aircraft. Connect industries, cities, and ports to maximize profit.
The Windows installer works out of the box with bundled open graphics and sound sets, so no original game files are needed. Online multiplayer lets you cooperate or compete with others.
/pages/software/windows/games/freeciv.ht: Free, turn-based empire-building strategy game inspired by Civilization.

FreeCiv is an open-source empire-building strategy game inspired by the Civilization series. Guide your civilization from the Stone Age to the Space Age, researching technologies, building cities, and waging diplomacy or war.
FreeCiv supports single-player vs. AI opponents and multiplayer over LAN or internet. Multiple rulesets let you play classic Civ1/Civ2 rules or modern variants.
/pages/software/windows/games/flightgear: Open-source flight simulator with realistic physics and scenery for Windows.

FlightGear is a sophisticated open-source flight simulator used by aviation enthusiasts and researchers alike. It models real-world physics, weather, and global scenery generated from NASA and SRTM elevation data.
Over 500 aircraft models are available, from the Cessna 172 to the Boeing 777. Multiplayer lets you fly with others on shared servers with ATC simulation.
/pages/software/linux/utility/tmux.html: Terminal multiplexer for splitting, managing, and persisting terminal sessions.
tmux lets you split a single terminal window into multiple panes, create named windows, and detach sessions so they keep running after you disconnect. Re-attach from any machine with tmux attach.
Server admins and developers rely on tmux to maintain long-running processes over SSH. Pair it with TPM (Tmux Plugin Manager) to add session persistence across reboots.
/pages/software/windows/utility/wireshar: Network protocol analyzer for Windows for packet capture and analysis.

Wireshark captures live network traffic via WinPcap/Npcap on Windows and lets you analyze every byte of every packet. Display filters let you narrow down to specific hosts, protocols, or error conditions.
TLS decryption with pre-master secrets, VoIP stream reassembly, and protocol statistics make it the most comprehensive network analysis tool available.
/pages/software/linux/utility/rsync.html: Fast, efficient file synchronization and backup tool for Linux.

rsync copies only the differences between source and destination, making incremental backups extremely fast. It works over SSH for secure remote sync and supports compression, checksums, and exclusion rules.
Common use cases include backup scripts, mirroring directories, and deploying websites. rsync is included in virtually every Linux distribution by default.
/pages/software/linux/utility/htop.html: Interactive process viewer and system monitor for Linux.

htop is an enhanced, color-coded replacement for the classic Unix top command. It shows CPU, memory, and swap usage per core, lists all processes, and lets you search, sort, and kill processes interactively.
Press F5 for a tree view of parent/child relationships. htop is available in every Linux distro's package manager and is the first utility most sysadmins install on a new server.
/pages/software/linux/utility/gparted.ht: Graphical partition editor for creating, resizing, and managing disk partitions.

GParted is the go-to graphical tool for partition management on Linux. It can create, delete, resize, move, copy, and check partitions on any block device. It supports ext4, NTFS, FAT32, Btrfs, XFS, and many more filesystems.
Available as a bootable live image for managing partitions without a running OS, or as a package in most Linux desktops.
/pages/software/linux/utility/gnupg.html: Open-source implementation of the OpenPGP standard for encryption and signing.

GnuPG (GPG) is the command-line OpenPGP implementation that underpins most Linux signing infrastructure. Use it to encrypt files, sign commits, verify package signatures, and manage a web of trust keyring.
Integrate GPG with Git for signed commits, with Thunderbird for encrypted email, and with password managers like Pass. It is pre-installed on most Linux distributions.
/pages/software/linux/productivity/libre: Full-featured free office suite for Linux with broad format support.

LibreOffice is the definitive open-source office suite for Linux. Writer, Calc, Impress, Draw, Base, and Math cover the full range of office productivity tasks. It reads and writes Microsoft Office formats with high fidelity.
Available in every major Linux distribution's package manager and as a Flatpak/Snap. The Document Foundation releases regular updates with improved compatibility and features.
/pages/software/linux/productivity/thund: Mozilla's free and open-source cross-platform email client.

Thunderbird is Mozilla's long-lived email client, now undergoing a renaissance with the Supernova redesign. It supports IMAP, POP3, SMTP, and multiple accounts. Built-in OpenPGP lets you encrypt email without installing plugins.
On Linux it integrates with GNOME and KDE calendaring via CalDAV. The extension ecosystem adds spam filtering, news feeds, and more.
/pages/software/linux/productivity/inksc: Professional SVG vector graphics editor for Linux.
Available in most repos and as a Flatpak/Snap. Its Python extension API is well-documented, enabling custom automation for production workflows.
GNU Image Manipulation Program — a professional image editor for Linux.

GIMP is the go-to raster image editor on Linux. It supports layers, masks, color spaces, scripts, and an enormous plugin library. Scripting with Script-Fu or Python automates repetitive editing tasks.
Available in every Linux distro's repos and as a Flatpak. GIMP 3.x brings GEGL-based non-destructive editing and improved color management.
/pages/software/linux/productivity/calib: Open-source e-book management and conversion tool for Linux.

Calibre is the ultimate e-book library manager. It organizes your collection, converts between formats (EPUB, MOBI, PDF, AZW3, and more), and can send books directly to e-readers. A built-in e-book viewer handles all major formats.
Calibre also supports news downloads from RSS feeds formatted as e-books. Its plugin system is extensive, covering DRM handling, metadata sources, and custom catalogs.
/pages/software/linux/games/xonotic.html: Fast-paced open-source arena first-person shooter for Linux.
Xonotic is a free, fast-paced first-person shooter built on the DarkPlaces engine. It focuses on arena-style gameplay with over 20 maps, multiple game modes, and bot support.
Developed as a fork of Nexuiz, Xonotic has an active community and regular updates. The game runs smoothly on most Linux hardware and supports keyboard-and-mouse or gamepad input.
/pages/software/linux/games/supertux.htm: Classic 2D platformer game inspired by Super Mario Bros for Linux.
SuperTux is a classic 2D side-scrolling platformer where you play as Tux the Linux penguin. It features over 100 levels across multiple worlds, with boss fights, secret areas, and a level editor.
Available in most Linux distribution repositories and as a Flatpak. The game is family-friendly and has been actively developed for over 20 years.
/pages/software/linux/games/openttd.html: Open-source transport simulation strategy game for Linux.

OpenTTD is an open-source reimplementation of Transport Tycoon Deluxe. Build rail, road, air, and sea transport networks to connect cities and deliver cargo. Manage finances, buy vehicles, and compete with AI companies.
Available via most Linux package managers and as a Flatpak. A thriving online community provides custom graphics sets, NewGRF extensions, and multiplayer servers.
/pages/software/linux/games/minetest.htm: Open-source voxel game engine and sandbox game for Linux.

Minetest is a free, open-source voxel game engine and sandbox game similar to Minecraft. It ships with a default game (Minetest Game) and supports hundreds of community mods that add new biomes, creatures, tools, and game rules.
Cross-platform and very light on system requirements, Minetest runs well even on older hardware. The Lua modding API is well-documented and beginner-friendly.
/pages/software/linux/games/0ad.html: Free, open-source real-time strategy game set in ancient history.
0 A.D. is a historically-based RTS game covering civilizations from 500 BC to 500 AD. It features detailed units, buildings, and technologies for factions like Greeks, Romans, Celts, and Persians.
Built on the Pyrogenesis engine, it supports skirmish, multiplayer, and scenario modes. Available as a Flatpak and in most Linux repos. Still in alpha but very playable.
/pages/software/apple/utility/keka.html: Free file archiver and extractor for macOS supporting many formats.
Keka is the most popular free file archiver on macOS. It supports extracting ZIP, RAR, 7z, TAR, GZIP, BZIP2, XZ, and many more formats, while creating archives in ZIP, 7z, and TAR.
It integrates with Finder via context menu actions and supports splitting archives and password protection. The source code is available on GitHub.
Network protocol analyzer for capturing and inspecting traffic on macOS.
Wireshark is the world's most widely used network packet analyzer. On macOS it captures live network traffic via pcap and lets you drill down into every field of every protocol from Ethernet to TLS.
Display filters, color coding, and stream following make it an indispensable tool for network debugging, security analysis, and protocol learning.
Open-source video transcoder for macOS supporting all major formats.

HandBrake converts video from nearly any format to modern codecs like H.264, H.265, VP9, and AV1. The macOS native build uses VideoToolbox hardware acceleration for fast, low-power encodes on Apple Silicon.
A built-in preset system covers everything from social media clips to archival quality. Batch queue processing lets you encode an entire folder while you step away.
/pages/software/apple/utility/balenaetch: Simple, cross-platform USB and SD card flash tool for macOS.
balenaEtcher makes flashing OS images to USB drives and SD cards foolproof. Select an image, select a target drive, and click Flash. It validates the write automatically to confirm integrity.
Particularly useful for flashing Linux distros, Raspberry Pi OS, or other embedded images. The Electron-based app runs identically on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
OpenPGP encryption and key management for macOS Mail and Finder.
GPG Suite integrates OpenPGP encryption into macOS Mail and Finder. Use it to sign and encrypt email, verify signed software downloads, and manage a keyring of trusted public keys.
GPG Keychain provides a graphical interface for generating, importing, exporting, and publishing keys to key servers. The command-line gpg tool is also included for scripting.
/pages/software/apple/productivity/vlc.h: Universal open-source media player for macOS supporting all formats.

VLC is the most versatile media player available, capable of playing almost any audio or video format without additional codecs. The macOS version supports GPU decoding, subtitles, audio tracks, and network streams.
Built by the VideoLAN non-profit, VLC contains no ads, no tracking, and no subscription. It also doubles as a simple media converter and streaming server.
/pages/software/apple/productivity/inksc: Professional open-source vector graphics editor for macOS.

Inkscape is a powerful SVG-based vector graphics editor. It supports paths, Bezier curves, text on path, pattern fills, gradients, and complex node editing. Inkscape files are native SVG, so they are web-ready by default.
It runs on macOS via XQuartz or natively with the GTK macOS port. Inkscape is widely used by designers, illustrators, and developers for logos, icons, and illustrations.
/pages/software/apple/productivity/libre: Full-featured free office suite compatible with Microsoft Office formats.
On macOS, LibreOffice runs natively and integrates with the system. It is developed by The Document Foundation and has a large, active contributor base.
/pages/software/apple/productivity/thund: Free, open-source email client from Mozilla for macOS.
Thunderbird is Mozilla's open-source email client with strong support for IMAP, POP3, and SMTP. It has a rich extension ecosystem including OpenPGP encryption support built in as of version 78.
The Supernova redesign brought a modern look and unified calendar, tasks, and email management in a single window. A great choice for power users who need full control over their email.
Powerful open-source image editor for macOS.

GIMP (GNU Image Manipulation Program) is a professional-grade image editor that runs on macOS. It supports layers, masks, curves, color correction, and a vast plugin ecosystem. GIMP can handle tasks traditionally done in Photoshop.
Script-Fu and Python-Fu scripting let you automate batch operations. A native macOS build with Apple Silicon support is available via the official site.
/pages/software/android/utility/wireguar: Modern, fast, and secure VPN protocol app for Android.

WireGuard is a state-of-the-art VPN protocol with a minimal codebase, making it far easier to audit than OpenVPN or IPSec. The Android app lets you connect to any WireGuard server by importing a config file or scanning a QR code.
With cryptokey routing and noise protocol, WireGuard provides excellent security while being significantly faster than legacy VPN protocols.
/pages/software/android/utility/termux.h: Terminal emulator and Linux environment for Android.

Termux is a powerful terminal emulator that brings a full Linux shell to Android without rooting. It supports a wide range of packages via its own apt repository — from Python and Node.js to Git and SSH.
Developers use Termux to run local servers, write scripts, and SSH into remote machines directly from their phone. The community maintains an extensive package ecosystem.
Android work profile manager to isolate and sandbox apps.

Shelter leverages Android's work profile feature to create an isolated space for apps you do not fully trust. Apps in the shelter profile cannot access your personal contacts, files, or location unless you permit it.
Use it to quarantine social media apps or ad-heavy apps while keeping your personal profile clean. No root required.
/pages/software/android/utility/fdroid.h: Free and open-source Android app store with no tracking.

F-Droid is an alternative app repository for Android that only hosts free and open-source software. Every app is built from source by F-Droid's build servers, so you can trust that no proprietary bits were inserted.
It includes anti-feature labels to warn you about ads, trackers, or non-free dependencies — something the Play Store never tells you.
/pages/software/android/productivity/tas: Powerful to-do list and task manager app for Android.
Tasks.org is a feature-rich task manager that supports Google Tasks and CalDAV sync. It offers due dates, reminders, subtasks, tags, filters, and location-based geofencing reminders.
The UI is clean and material-design compliant. Being open-source and CalDAV-compatible means your tasks are never locked into a proprietary silo.
/pages/software/android/productivity/sig: Private messaging app with end-to-end encryption for Android.

Signal is the gold standard for private, end-to-end encrypted messaging. It supports text, voice calls, video calls, and file sharing. Signal collects almost no metadata and its protocol is open and independently audited.
Designed for everyday users who value privacy, Signal is a drop-in replacement for SMS and MMS with a familiar interface.
/pages/software/android/productivity/org: Outline notes and tasks app for Android using Org-mode format.
Orgzly brings Emacs Org-mode to Android. It lets you manage hierarchical notes and to-do lists stored as plain .org text files. Files sync via any cloud provider that supports file sync.
It supports scheduling, priorities, tags, and search queries, making it a powerful tool for GTD-style task management on mobile.
/pages/software/android/productivity/mar: Markdown and plain-text editor for Android with preview support.

Markor is a versatile text editor focused on Markdown. It supports live preview, syntax highlighting, to-do lists, and a link-based wiki mode. Files are stored as plain text so they are portable across any tool.
Markor integrates well with sync folders from Syncthing or cloud storage, making it ideal for note-taking on Android.
/pages/software/android/utility/adaway.h: Open-source system-wide ad blocker for Android using hosts file.
AdAway blocks ads system-wide by redirecting known ad domains to localhost via the hosts file. It works across all apps and browsers, not just a single browser extension.
A root mode gives full system-wide blocking, while a VPN mode works without root. The hosts sources are community maintained and regularly updated.
/pages/software/android/productivity/ant: Open-source podcast manager and player for Android.
AntennaPod is a fully featured podcast manager with no ads and no tracking. Add feeds from any RSS source, subscribe to podcasts, download episodes for offline listening, and control playback speed.
It supports OPML import/export, making it easy to migrate from other podcast apps. Available on F-Droid for a fully open supply chain.

Git Workflows Every Developer Should Know
Why Workflow Matters More Than Commands
A practical breakdown of the most important Git workflows: feature branches, Gitflow, trunk-based development, and more.

The simplest useful workflow: every new feature or bug fix gets its own branch off main . When the work is ready, open a pull request, get a review, and merge. The main branch always reflects deployable code.

This works well for small teams and is the baseline most other workflows build on. The key discipline is keeping feature branches short-lived — ideally merged within a day or two — to minimize merge conflicts.
Gitflow suits products with scheduled release cycles and parallel version maintenance. It is overkill for continuous-delivery web apps, where trunk-based development is a better fit.

TBD requires strong CI: every commit triggers a full test suite, and broken builds block merges. When it works, it produces the fastest feedback loops and the lowest merge conflict rate of any workflow.
Choose one strategy per repository and enforce it consistently. Mixing strategies makes git log and git bisect confusing.

Set up GPG commit signing early if your team requires it. GnuPG is usually pre-installed; generate a key, add it to GitHub, and configure Git to sign commits automatically with git config --global commit.gpgsign true .

Linux follows the Filesystem Hierarchy Standard: binaries in /usr/bin , config in /etc , user homes in /home , and temporary files in /tmp . Understanding where things live helps when debugging PATH issues or setting up services.
